Slow extraction

Who keeps selling into every new wave of buyers?

9 chapters with worked investigations

01Thesis vs hygiene02Immediate rug risk03Slow extraction04Organic slow death05The self rug06Token cycle, meta cycle & attention07Due diligence keeps moving08Clear decision states09The basic dev view

01Definition

Planned slow-rug behavior extracts value over time through recurring distribution, transfers, or liquidity removal.

02Why it matters

Extraction can unfold over hours, days, or longer while a lively chart consumes incoming demand.

03What to check

  • Related inventory, transfers, and repeated sales over time
  • Selling around attention spikes and failed rebounds
  • Liquidity changes and evidence connecting suspected wallets

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Ownership broadens and fresh demand absorbs observable selling.

Dangerous

A suspected cluster repeatedly extracts value while exit depth weakens.

05Beginner mistake

Treating fresh addresses as independent owners.

06Takeaway

Follow the inventory, not just the pump.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

Suppose linked wallets begin with 30 million units. Over three promotions they sell 4m, 3m, and 5m, and transfer 6m between themselves. Group inventory falls to 18m, not 12m: internal transfers do not remove supply from the group. Continued selling is measurable; malicious intent is a separate claim.

How to investigate it

Create an address ledger with opening balances, purchases, sales, external transfers, and closing balances. Match actual swaps to attention spikes using timestamps. Include receiving addresses when linkage is justified. Compare remaining supply with current depth and quote sizes; a smaller visible creator balance can hide unchanged group control.

Check your reasoning — answered

The creator balance falls from 10m to 2m, while a supported linked address receives 8m. How much group inventory disappeared? Zero through that transfer. Investigate subsequent swaps before claiming the group sold 8m.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Inspect

Look for repeated observed selling. Trace funding, transfers, remaining supply, and ownership externally; sampled flow cannot prove coordination or intent.

Go deeper

Common funding is a lead, not proof: exchange customers can share a funding source. Combine transfers, timing, balances, and repeated behavior. Estimated cost basis can miss earlier trades or transfers. Falling balances may reflect a transfer rather than a sale; keep those events separate.
